region_scene_page.compact: Americana and country-folk grew around artists who used older roots materials without fitting neatly into commercial country or pure folk revival categories.
region_scene_page.standard: Americana and country-folk grew around artists who used older roots materials without fitting neatly into commercial country or pure folk revival categories. John Prine's Sam Stone, Steve Earle's Guitar Town, Lucinda Williams, and Kris Kristofferson's Sunday Mornin' Comin' Down give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: Americana and country-folk grew around artists who used older roots materials without fitting neatly into commercial country or pure folk revival categories. The center is the song and voice, with twang used as a storytelling texture rather than a commercial format marker. John Prine's Sam Stone, Steve Earle's Guitar Town, Lucinda Williams, and Kris Kristofferson's Sunday Mornin' Comin' Down give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.
